summary: Elastic batcher fragmentation causing intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes for short single-sequence requests
description: Issue summary: FinSight reports intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes (up to 2.4s from ~220ms baseline) for short single-sequence text-generation requests in their dedicated pool. Spikes occur sporadically during steady low-to-medium QPS (20-40 qps) and correlate with periods when the elastic batcher splits requests into many small micro-batches rather than forming one optimal batch. Impact: Customer-facing application experiences delayed responses and occasional upstream request timeouts (504) causing customer support tickets. Environment: Dedicated pool (FinSight-reserved), serving-runtime v2.9.1, continuous-batcher configured with adaptive shard sizing and elastic fragmentation enabled. Timeline: First observed 2026-03-09 15:14 UTC, recurring through 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-11. Triage: P1 due to customer business impact (analytics dashboard timeouts).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use FinSight dedicated config (adaptive-shard=true, elastic-fragmentation=true) in prod-like pool.
2) Send sustained low-medium QPS synthetic load: 25 qps of short requests (avg token output 12, prompt length ~30).
3) Observe latency distribution on per-request traces and server-side batch metrics for 30+ minutes.
4) Notice periodic episodes where batching splits into 6-10 micro-batches for a small window, and p95/p99 spike for affected requests.

comments: Priya Desai (Support) [2026-03-10]: Received several escalations from FinSight CS. Collected traces and initial serving logs; opening ticket—assigning to runtime oncall.

Marco Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-10]: Confirmed p99 spikes in FinSight pool. Initial correlation with elastic-fragmentation metric. Added debug flags to continuous-batcher on two nodes for deeper sampling.
FinSight Ops (Customer) [2026-03-10]: We see dashboard timeouts around the same timestamps. Request samples attached in customer email (ref: email thread id 3421).
Marco Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Deployed temporary mitigation: force-fragmentation=false for FinSight pool. Early telemetry shows reduction in p99 spikes during a 2-hour window.
Priya Desai (Support) [2026-03-11]: Customer confirmed fewer timeouts after mitigation but requests still show occasional elevated p95; they want root cause and permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Elastic fragmentation heuristic is over-fragmenting for mixed-length short-sequence workloads, creating head-of-line micro-batch stalls.
Hypothesis 2: Recent scheduler change (commit 3b9d7f2) that aggressively shards idle connections interacts poorly with fragmenter backoff window.
Findings: Flamegraphs show CPU idle periods between micro-batch flushes; batch topology logs show many small fragments instead of a cohesive batch when sequence length variance is low.
Metric correlation: frag_ratio spikes align with p99 spikes (frag_ratio > 0.6 -> p99 increases x6).
Reproduction: Reproduced at lower scale in staging by enabling elastic fragmentation and simulating FinSight payload distribution—observed same micro-batch pattern.
Related code paths: continuous-batcher/fragmenter.cpp:fragment_decision() uses time-based backoff that does not account for recent flush jitter introduced in scheduler commit 3b9d7f2.
Runbook references: batcher-fragmentation runbook suggests toggle but warns about perf regressions—documented in linked Confluence page.
resolution: Mitigation applied: forced elastic-fragmentation=false for FinSight dedicated pool (temporary) which reduced p99 spikes and eliminated user-facing 504s. Root cause: interaction between fragmenter backoff logic and new scheduler idle-shrink behaviour causing over-fragmentation windows. Permanent fix plan: PR to adjust fragment_decision() to include recent_flush_jitter metric and lower fragmentation sensitivity (PR #2148 opened). Rollout plan: staged deploy to dedicated pools with canary traffic (5% -> 25% -> 100%) over 48 hours. Post-deploy monitoring: add frag_ratio alert and p95/p99 baseline regression test to Redwood Optimize recommendations for dedicated customers. Follow-ups: create INT ticket to audit other dedicated pools for similar config (INT-4120), update runbook with explicit guidance for 'elastic-fragmentation' flag.
